title: Windows: review_freeze_cli test target warns "unused import super::*" in src/test_temp_paths.rs:5 after the include! migration
outcome: Windows B's registered FULL on ebc30de9 (test-775069d9, PASS, relay #848, 07:45Z) shows one warning in the integration test target review_freeze_cli: "warning: unused import: `super::*` --> tests\../src/test_temp_paths.rs:5:5". This warning was not in the retained S0 (bd01930c) Windows FULL baseline log. Since the migration (w-f621028c8a08), src/test_temp_paths.rs opens with `use super::*;`. It is a module of the binary (src/main.rs:1269), and tests/review_freeze_cli.rs:12 also pastes it with include!("../src/test_temp_paths.rs"). In that include context, on Windows, the glob import is unused. The bin warning counts are still at the 7/27 baseline. Outcome: the review_freeze_cli target compiles on Windows without this warning, by giving the include site the imports it needs or by narrowing the glob, and the binary's module behaviour is unchanged. Provenance: filed by Opus2 from Windows B's run report. It is not a gate failure.
acceptance: Windows: review_freeze_cli test target warns "unused import super::*" in src/test_temp_paths.rs:5 after the include! migration is done
